pr_body:
A driver for sql.js based on the AbstractSqliteDriver.
Two things I'm not quiet sure about yet:
**Naming**
is there a better way than calling it `SqljsDriver`?

**Import/Export**
Since the database in sql.js is never persisted the library supports an import/export mechanism. The problem with that is, that the database to import has to passed to the constructor in `createDatabaseConnection`. Therefore the only option I could come up with was use an option field (`databaseForImport`) which can be set to `new Uint8Array(0)` if nothing should be imported.
And with
```ts
connection.driver as any;
driver.export();
```
the database can be exported. Is there a nicer way for the import and maybe even the export?

Tested in the browser, but should also work in node.js

closes #822
pr_comments:
What if we implement following options:

1. Automatically manage database saving for user. When he connects we read from a provided database (from connection options). Each time when he saves/inserts/removes/updates something we save database (how to save it defined in connection options too)

2. Provide mechanizm for a user to manage saving by his own. For example:

```ts
connection.importDatabase(...); // or maybe call it loadDatabase or some better name
```
and
```
connection.exportDatabase(...); // or some better name
```

> connection.driver as any;
driver.export();

Too dirty for users. I would like to avoid adding sqljs-specific methods to connection, however using "any" or any other casting isnt an option. Alternative is to make things like in mongo - create `SqljsEntityManager` (like `MongoEntityManager`) and add there two new methods for export and import. Also we'll need to create `getSqljsManager` method in `index.ts` Actually I like it more then what Ive suggested before to add it in connection (including the fact how often sqljs will be used its a very pragmatic and elegant solution).

> is there a better way than calling it SqljsDriver

Probably yes. Alternative is to name it SqlJSDriver, but Im not sure if its better.

> Tested in the browser, but should also work in node.js

we need to include it in ormconfig.dist / ormconfig.travis to run then in nodejs as well. Also probably we'll need to include tests enabled only for this driver which cover this specific functionality (option to auto save or option to provided place)

>  Therefore the only option I could come up with was use an option field (databaseForImport) which can be set to new Uint8Array(0) if nothing should be imported.

Im not sure I completely understood this part.... But we need to make things flexible and easy for users. For example user needs to be able to provide simply path, like "/test/db.sql" and it should be automatically handled (for nodejs it may save database in file system and for browser it can save it in local storage). What do you think about it, is it implementable? This does not exclude option to provide utf8array too.
Thanks for your feedback. I really like your ideas! I will see what I can do
@daniel-lang any updates on this PR?

I wasn't comfortable digging that deep into TypeORM, so I waited a bit to get more familiar with TypeORM. I hope, that I can update it this weekend or early next week so that it can be part of the 0.1 release

@pleerock I push the most recent ideas.
As you suggested I added a special entity manager so functions like `loadDatabase()`, `saveDatabase()` and `exportDatabase()` can be called easily.
For autosave, I thought it might be a good idea to use an interval and leave it to the user to decide how often he wants his database saved. There are two options `autoSave` (enable it) and `autoSaveInterval` to configure it.

This is still missing:
* [ ] docs
* [ ] tests

Tests for `load`, `export` and `save` exist now.

How do you want to do the autoSave feature?
- Like it is right know with two options (enable and interval)
- Like you suggested with one option (what would be the interval if it's just set to true?)
- Like you originally suggested, where it would save after every query

as for me interval does not make lot of sense. Database needs to be saved only after some modifications are applied on it, right? And usually modifications aren't so often, so saving database on that point kinda makes sense. Plus interval isn't reliable - in browser, what if interval is high (and making it low does not make sense because there are lot of reads and much less writes), what if user just closes the window and interval time isn't reached.
Also we'll need to create a good facade/interface for users to easily configure how it gonna autosave (where?)

Okay, I will rewrite the autosave part to save after insert, update and delete.

>Also we'll need to create a good facade/interface for users to easily configure how it gonna autosave 

What do you want the user to configure other than enable it and the location (both of them have an option)?

> What do you want the user to configure other than enable it and the location (both of them have an option)?

Do you mean location like `"/test/db.sql"` ? If yes, then can we implement it? Should be yes in nodejs, but what about browser? Shall we store it someone in the local storage? What about if user wants to save using his own method, how do he configure it?

The way it's implemented right now is:
- location option
   - nodejs: specify a file location like "/test/db.sql"
   - browser: specify the localstorage key to use (used like `localstorage.setItem(location, database)`)
- users can call `SqljsEntityManager.exportDatabase()` at any time and get the current database, but defining your one method that gets called on autosave is not support right now. But I like the idea
